jobs.title: Flatiron Research Fellow - Developmental Dynamics, Center for Computational Biology
jobs.institution: Flatiron Institute - Simons Foundation
jobs.description:
The Center for Computational Biology (CCB) of the Simons Foundation’s Flatiron Institute is actively seeking enthusiastic, full-time post-doctoral Flatiron Research Fellows to join its Developmental Dynamics Group. Candidates interested in data-driven modeling of biological systems, especially in the context of behavioral changes during postembryonic development, are encouraged to apply, as are those with strong backgrounds in dynamical systems theory, biophysical theory, statistics, and machine learning.
ABOUT THE CENTER FOR COMPUTATIONAL BIOLOGY : CCB has a twofold mission: to develop the rigorous modeling tools and theory needed for understanding biological processes, and to create computational frameworks that will facilitate the analysis of the large, complex data sets being generated by quantitative experimental technologies. To accomplish this, CCB brings together experts in various biological domains (including genomics, molecular, cellular, and developmental biology) whose approaches are informed by the modern computational tools of applied mathematics, statistical inference, artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML), biophysics, and computer science. The goal: to enable CCB to undertake ambitious, long-term research projects that transcend conventional disciplinary boundaries and that lead to a quantitative and predictive understanding of biological phenomena; and to develop high-quality, well-tested, versatile and extensible software across its research areas.
CCB currently comprises more than 50 scientists at career stages from Ph.Ds through senior scientists, as well as visiting scientists and guest researchers, affiliated graduate students and interns. Together, the CCB scientific staff are pioneering an approach to biology in which theory,computation, and experimentation are integrated, from problem conceptualization onwards. This approach enables CCB to tackle not only recognized, fundamental problems in biology that have so far eluded solution, but also, because of the value placed on curiosity-driven research, to find and develop new areas of biological inquiry.
ABOUT THE DEVELOPMENTAL DYNAMICS GROUP : The Developmental Dynamics group, combines experiments, theory and computing to elucidate the contributions of encoded genomic instructions and self-organizing physical mechanisms to embryonic development. Its theoretical and computational work is designed to integrate and abstract rapidly accumulating heterogeneous datasets, to propose critical tests of multiscale regulatory mechanisms, and to guide our own genetic and imaging experiments. The group’s research is organized around three main themes: the mechanistic modeling of pattern formation and morphogenesis; the synthesis and decomposition of developmental trajectories; and the modeling of human developmental abnormalities, including structural defects and puberty disorders.
POSITION DESCRIPTION
Flatiron Research Fellows in CCB are individuals at the postdoctoral level with backgrounds in one or more of the following areas: computational biology, computer science, applied mathematics, computational biology, biophysics, computer science, engineering, mathematical physics, or related disciplines.
Reporting to Research Scientists, Data Scientists or the Center Director, as appropriate, Fellows are expected to carry out an active research program that can be independently directed and/or involve substantial collaboration with other members of CCB or the Flatiron Institute. In addition to their research, Fellows help build the rich scientific community at CCB and the Flatiron Institute by participating in seminars, colloquia, and group meetings; developing their software, mathematical and computational expertise through internal education opportunities; and sharing their knowledge through scientific publications, presentations, and/or software releases, with the financial support of the Institute. Fellows have access to the Flatiron Institute’s powerful scientific computing resources.
Responsibilities include but are not limited to:
Performing theoretical and computational research
Developing, implementing and maintaining scientific software
Participating in the organization of CCB and Flatiron-wide collaborative activities including seminars, workshops and meetings
Participating in the preparation of manuscripts for publication and of presentations at scientific conferences
Assisting in student mentorship
Sharing expertise and providing training and guidance to CCB staff and visitors as needed.
Fellows will be based, and have a principal office or workspace, at the Simons Foundation’s offices in New York City. The initial appointments for Flatiron Research Fellows are generally for two years, with the possibility of renewal for a third year, contingent on performance. FRFs may be eligible for subsidized housing within walking distance of CCB.
The start date is flexible, with the Fellow expected to begin no later than September 2027.
For more information about careers at the Flatiron Institute, please click here.

jobs.title: Assistant, Associate or Professor WOT (Pediatric Pain Psychologist) - Anesthesiology & Pain Medicine, Seattle Children's Hospital
jobs.institution: University of Washington: Anesthesiology and Pain Medicine
jobs.description:
The University of Washington (UW) School of Medicine Department of Anesthesiology and Pain Medicine at Seattle Children’s Hospital (SCH) is seeking a pediatric psychologist for the Pain Medicine program with an anticipated start date of February 2027 or thereafter. We seek applicants who demonstrate commitment to excellence in clinical service, teaching, and research in a diverse and inclusive academic community.
Seattle Children’s provides care to children from the WWAMI (Washington, Wyoming, Alaska, Montana, and Idaho) region and supports pediatric surgical and medical specialties. Responsibilities in the interdisciplinary Pediatric Pain Program include psychological assessment and treatment services in the outpatient pain clinic, pain rehabilitation program, and inpatient consultation service. There are opportunities for interprofessional teaching and collaborative research in the Pediatric Pain and Sleep Innovation Lab at the Center for Child Health Behavior and Development, Seattle Children’s Research Institute (SCRI). This position features an academic appointment through the UW Department of Anesthesiology and Pain Medicine, a close affiliate of SCH and SCRI. As one of the nation’s top ranked medical schools and research institutions, our faculty benefit from being part of an expansive academic department of over 260 faculty members and 160 residents and fellow trainees across its clinical sites. University of Washington faculty engage in teaching research/scholarship and service.
The successful candidate will join our faculty on a full-time basis for a twelve-month appointment. Assistant Professors are eligible for multi-year appointments that align with a 12-month service period (e.g., July 1-June 30). Associate Professors and Professors hold indefinite appointments that align with a 12-month service period (e.g., July 1-June 30). Faculty with 12-month service periods are paid for 11 months of service over a 12-month period (July-June), with the equivalent of one month is available for paid time off. These positions are without tenure due to funding. Salary and academic appointment at University of Washington will be commensurate with experience, qualifications, and academic rank. The base salary range will be: Assistant Professor $11,667 - $12,500 per month ($140,004 - $150,000 annually), Associate Professor $13,334 - $14,167 per month ($160,008 – $170,004 annually), and Professor $14,667 - $15,584 ($176,004 - $187,008 annually), commensurate with experience and qualifications, or as mandated by a US Department of Labor prevailing wage determination. This range is inclusive of base salary provided through the Children’s University Medical Group (CUMG) practice plan, in addition to base salary provided by the University. Please note that only compensation provided by the University is included in University benefit determinations and calculations. Other compensation associated with this position may include incentive through the CUMG practice plan. Compensation provided by the CUMG practice plan may provide eligibility for separate benefits offered by that organization. For practitioners holding an appointment in the physicians practice plans, see the link for additional benefits that may be available at CUMG: https://faculty.uwmedicine.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/CUMG-Benefits-Summary-for-recruiting.pdf

jobs.title: Open Rank: Assistant Professor/Associate Professor/Professor of Psychiatry (General Psychiatry - Tenure Track)
jobs.institution: Columbia University in the City of New York: Psychiatry
jobs.description:
The Department of Psychiatry at Columbia University Irving Medical Center invites applications for a tenure-track or tenure-track equivalent full-time faculty positions. The successful candidate will contribute to the department's mission by engaging in high-impact research. Candidates with a Ph.D., M.D./Ph.D., or M.D. will be considered at all levels of seniority (Assistant, Associate, and Full Professor). Research programs can investigate topics relevant to any area of mental health and psychiatry across the lifespan, ranging from childhood, to adolescence, adulthood, and older adulthood (geriatrics). Research approaches may include, but are not limited to:
Neuroscience research aimed at revealing mechanisms at molecular, cellular, developmental, circuit, systems, and/or computational levels of analysis in model systems and/or humans, including genetic and genomic approaches.
Pathophysiology and experimental therapeutics research using translational, computational and/or imaging approaches in animals or humans to elucidate disease and therapeutic mechanisms and to test novel treatments, including pharmacological, neuromodulatory and psychosocial interventions.
Epidemiology, prevention and health services research that uses large population and clinical data along with novel causal inference methods to inform our understanding of the development, determinants, expression and treatment of psychiatric disorders across the lifespan and across populations, including global mental health.
Community-partnered implementation research and practice that focuses on improving health and behavioral health outcomes for individuals receiving services in real-world care and community settings.
All mental health and psychiatric conditions, including their intersection with health and the influence of social determinants, are of potential interest, including but not limited to mood, anxiety and psychotic disorders, disorders affecting cognition, child and neurodevelopmental disorders, disorders arising in geriatric patient populations, substance use disorders, eating disorders, and suicidal behavior.
The successful candidate will join a highly dedicated community that offers extraordinary clinical, educational, and research resources. The position offers opportunities for collaboration with multidisciplinary teams in a dynamic academic research and clinical environment. For more information on the Department of Psychiatry, visit our website.
Applicants should submit a letter of application, curriculum vitae, short research and teaching statements, 2-3 key publications, and 3 letters of recommendation. Applications will begin to be evaluated November 1, 2026.

jobs.title: Open Rank: Assistant Professor/Associate Professor/Professor of Psychiatry (Computational Psychiatry - Tenure Track)
jobs.institution: Columbia University in the City of New York: Psychiatry
jobs.description:
The Department of Psychiatry at Columbia University is inviting applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the assistant to full professor level. We seek candidates whose research is focused on computational approaches to understand neurocognitive mechanisms of psychiatric disorders. Expertise in theory-driven cognitive paradigms and computational analysis of neurofunctional (e.g., fMRI/EEG) and behavioral data is required, along with strong skills in advanced data-driven methods. Emphasis on translation into clinical applications and bridging preclinical to clinical work is strongly preferred. The successful candidate will be engaged in multidisciplinary, translational, collaborative work with clinical and preclinical researchers within and beyond the Department, who are studying related processes in humans and non-human model systems across the lifespan. Candidates will have a background in psychiatry, neuroscience, psychology, or related areas (holding an MD, MD/PhD, PhD or equivalent degree) and should have, or demonstrate strong potential to obtain, sustained extramural funding to support an independent research program. We encourage members of minority groups, women, persons with disabilities, and covered veterans to apply. Applicants should send a letter of application, curriculum vitae, short research and teaching statements, 2-3 key publications, and arrange for 3-5 letters of recommendation.
The successful candidate will join a highly dedicated community that offers extraordinary clinical, educational, and research resources. The position offers opportunities for collaboration with multidisciplinary teams in a dynamic academic research and clinical environment. For more information on the Department of Psychiatry, visit our website.
Please note that suggested salary ranges are subject to adjustment based on professional rank and a number of additional factors.

jobs.title: Research Associate - Cichon Lab

jobs.description:

jobs.title: STPH Faculty Associate/Academic Associate Pool AY26-27
jobs.institution: Arizona State University: School of Technology for Public Health
jobs.description:
Position Description:
Essential Functions
Academic Associates and Faculty Associates support undergraduate and graduate courses, as assigned and consistent with their qualifications. Courses may be offered in person, online, or in a hybrid format.
Responsibilities Applicable to Both Positions
Communicate regularly and professionally with students and faculty.
Respond to student questions within established course and program timelines.
Use learning management systems, instructional technology, and online communication tools effectively.
Promote a positive and supportive learning environment.
Participate in required meetings, training, and course-related activities.
Seek guidance and elevate student or course concerns when appropriate.
Complete assigned responsibilities throughout the full duration of the appointment.
Academic Associate Responsibilities
Academic Associates support courses under the direction of the faculty instructor. Duties may include:
Evaluating student work, assigning grades, and providing constructive feedback as directed by the faculty instructor.
Moderating discussion boards and facilitating other course activities as assigned.
Maintaining ongoing communication with the faculty instructor throughout the course, which may include regular synchronous Zoom meetings during business hours.
Meeting synchronously (via Zoom) with students individually or in small groups as needed to assist with mastery of course content.
Responding to student inquiries and forwarding student communications to the faculty instructor within 24 business hours.
Assisting with assignments, assessments, course materials, and other course-related responsibilities.
Faculty Associate Responsibilities
Faculty Associates teach assigned courses and are responsible for the instructional delivery of those courses. Duties may include:
Teaching undergraduate or graduate courses, as assigned and consistent with the Faculty Associate’s qualifications, in an in-person, online, or hybrid format.
Developing or adapting syllabi, lectures, course materials, assignments, and assessments in accordance with approved curricula, course objectives, and program requirements.
Evaluating student performance, assigning grades, and providing timely and constructive feedback.
Maintaining regular availability to students, including holding office hours appropriate to the course modality.
Monitoring student success and regularly responding to student academic issues.
Maintaining accurate course records and submitting grades and other required materials by established deadlines.
STPH invites applications to establish a pool of instructional Academic Associates and Faculty Associates for the 2026/2027 academic year. Successful candidates will support online or in-person courses under the direction of STPH faculty, evaluate student work, communicate regularly with students and the instructional team and assist students with mastery of course objectives. STPH welcomes applications from candidates who align with the Arizona State University (ASU) Charter and are committed to excellence and student success.
Faculty Associate and Academic Associate positions are one semester (8 or 16 weeks), non-benefits-eligible, and fixed-term appointments with no tenure implications, not to exceed .40 full-time equivalency (FTE). Individuals hired must be available for the entire duration of the appointment (8 or 16 weeks). The number of courses is contingent upon needs, funding, and sufficient student enrollment. Individuals hired as Faculty Associates and Academic Associates may not hold multiple, non-benefits-eligible appointments at ASU. Salary is a flat rate based on FTE.
This recruitment is to establish a part-time hiring pool for temporary and semester appointments. Applications are considered for the current academic year only. Applicants who are not hired are encouraged to reapply for subsequent academic years.
About the School:
The School of Technology for Public Health (STPH) is establishing a new field to reimagine public health infrastructure in the 21st century, and create more integrative, responsive, and resilient systems to protect the health of people in Arizona and beyond. Designed in collaboration with national leaders and informed by listening sessions with local communities and health departments, the school is the first of its kind in the nation to train students to be bilingual in public health and technology. By teaching students to be “techno-fluent,” the school serves as a catalyst to build and deploy the products, programs and systems needed to sculpt the future of public health in this decade and beyond.
STPH is part of an exciting, vibrant, and varied research, education, and practice community at ASU, which was named by U.S. News and World Report repeatedly as #1 in Innovation among all universities in the United States.
About Arizona State University:
Arizona State University, ranked the No. 1 “Most Innovative School” in the nation by U.S. News & World Report for twelve years in succession, has forged the model for a New American University. Year after year, ASU ranks at or near the top of the list in areas that matter. ASU is a comprehensive public research institution, measured not by whom it excludes, but by whom it includes and how they succeed; advancing research and discovery of public value; and assuming fundamental responsibility for the economic, social, cultural and overall health of the communities it serves. ASU operates on the principles that learning is a personal and original journey for each student; that they thrive on experience and that the process of discovery cannot be bound by traditional academic disciplines. Through innovation and a commitment to accessibility, ASU has drawn pioneering researchers to its faculty even as it expands opportunities for qualified students, attracting some of the highest- quality students from all 50 states and more than 130 nations.
All we do at ASU is guided and inspired by the ASU Charter, which reads:
ASU is a comprehensive public research university, measured not by whom it excludes, but by whom it includes and how they succeed; advancing research and discovery of public value; and assuming fundamental responsibility for the economic, social, cultural and overall health of the communities it serves.
Successful candidates will demonstrate throughout their materials how their teaching and service will contribute to the fulfillment of this Charter.

An interest in health outcomes, health disparities, or translational research is desirable.
For additional information about the position, please contact Dr. Christopher Kramer, Chief, Division of Cardiovascular Medicine, via email at CMK2N@virginia.edu or phone 434-982-0853.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Design, Department of Art and Art History
jobs.institution: Georgetown University: Art and Art History
jobs.description:
The Department of Art and Art History at Georgetown University invites applications for a tenure-track assistant professor position to begin in August 2027. The teaching load is two undergraduate courses per semester. Candidates will demonstrate the potential for excellence in research / creative work and teaching and will have completed an MFA in Graphic Design or a closely related field by the start date of the position.
The successful candidate will be able to teach undergraduate courses in graphic design and/or closely related subjects, have demonstrated proficiency with the tools and technologies used in these areas, knowledge of contemporary issues and emerging technologies in screen-based and material visual design, and an established practice as a designer. We especially welcome interdisciplinary approaches that demonstrate critically engaged teaching, research, and practice.Such approaches may include but are not limited to art theory, visual studies, communication design, design history, maker spaces, and interdisciplinary humanities and sciences. An inventive, experimental colleague in this position will be able to collaborate within and beyond the Department of Art and Art History, and to inspire students to engage reflectively with the powerful roles of design in society.
Qualifications:
MFA or equivalent in graphic design or a closely related field
Experience in undergraduate teaching at introductory and higher levels
Active research / creative practice in the field
Demonstrated proficiency with current and emerging technologies of design
Application Instructions:
Click on Apply Now to submit the following required materials:
1. Concise cover letter addressing relevant experience, research / creative work, teaching, and reasons for applying to Georgetown
2. CV
3. A selected portfolio (URL or single pdf) of the applicant’s research /creative work and up to 10 images of student work, if available
4. One original syllabus including a brief course description
5. A list of three references (reference letters are not required at this stage)
Applications are due by December 7, 2026
For questions related to this position, please contact: Prof. Alfred Acres, Department Chair - Alfred.Acres@georgetown.edu
The projected base salary range is $85,058 – $100,946. Compensation is determined by a number of factors including, but not limited to, the candidate’s individual qualifications, experience, education, skills, and certifications, as well as the University’s business needs and external factors.

jobs.title: Part-Time Lecturer (non-tenure track) for Bio 134 – Neurobiology

jobs.description: The Department of Biology at Tufts University seeks a part-time, non-tenure track faculty member to teach a neurobiology course (Bio 134 – Neurobiology) in the spring of 2027 (mid-January to mid-May). The course should cover the biology of nervous systems and may include topics such as the biophysical basis of neuronal function, synaptic interactions and signal processing in neural circuits, behavior, learning, and memory. jobs.title: Assistant Professor, Mathematics
jobs.institution: University of Washington: Mathematics
jobs.description:
The Department of Mathematics at the University of Washington invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor, with an anticipated start date of September 16, 2027. This position will provide successful candidates the opportunity to tackle the grand challenge of defining the shape of mathematics and mathematics research in response to rapid change and tremendous opportunity.
Located in one of the most dynamic and beautiful areas in the United States, the University of Washington is a premier research university, frequently cited as one of the best in the world. The Department of Mathematics is one of the top mathematics departments among public universities in the United States. The university and its surroundings abound with opportunities to do interdisciplinary research, engage in community-focused research, education, and service, and collaborate with private and governmental organizations. The Seattle metropolitan area provides abundant culinary, cultural, recreational, and educational resources and experiences.
All University of Washington faculty are expected to engage in teaching, research, and service.

jobs.title: Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor of Musculoskeletal Imaging

jobs.description:

Clinical responsibilities in Centreville, Virginia will involve reading of studies performed at the UVA Medical Center, the new UVA Orthopedic Center on Ivy Road and other affiliated imaging centers. On-site readings are performed at the new UVA Health Outpatient Imaging Centreville. Clinical responsibilities in Charlottesville, Virginia will require an on-site presence at the UVA Medical Center and Ivy Orthopedic Center to assist with musculoskeletal imaging procedures and teaching responsibilities.
Centreville, Virginia is a major bedroom community in Northern Virginia with a population of roughly 71,000-73,500 people. The area is known for its diverse population with strong Fairfax County Public Schools, family-oriented planned neighborhoods, shopping centers, parks, and convenient access to major Virginia routes such as I-66, Route 28, and U.S. 29. Lifestyle is classic suburban living – car dependent, with good amenities, but still within commuting distance of Washington, D.C. For more information about the Centreville, Virginia outpatient center, along with Centreville proper, please see: https://www.centrevilleimaging.com/ and https://www.fxva.com/explore/discover-neighborhoods/centreville/.
Charlottesville, Virginia, is consistently ranked by media outlets as one of the best places in the United States to live, work, and raise a family. Local residents enjoy everything that a major metropolitan area has to offer in an easygoing small city nestled in the foothills of the Blue Ridge Mountains. The Charlottesville area has excellent public and private schools and diverse housing options as well as sophisticated food, beverage, music and art scenes. jobs.title: Path 1 Kawader: Research Assistant – Wireless Communications
jobs.institution: New York University: Abu Dhabi
jobs.description:
NYUAD Wireless Center invites applications for a Kawader Research Assistant position to work on the development of cutting-edge wireless communication technologies.
The successful candidate will be responsible for the end-to-end design, implementation, and experimental validation of wireless communication systems using software-defined radio (SDR) platforms. The role will involve developing complete transmitter and receiver chains, implementing physical layer signal processing algorithms, integrating hardware and software components, and conducting over-the-air experiments. The candidate will contribute to the development of experimental testbeds supporting research on emerging 6G wireless communication technologies.
What the Program Offers
Full-time paid research position for up to 3 years.
Mentorship by internationally recognized NYUAD faculty members and researchers.
Professional development and academic training opportunities.
Exposure to interdisciplinary and collaborative research projects.
Support in preparing for graduate school applications.
Hands-on research experience in wireless communications, software-defined radio, signal processing, and emerging 6G technologies.
Experience designing, implementing, and experimentally validating advanced wireless communication systems.
Key Responsibilities
Design, implement, and experimentally validate wireless communication systems using software-defined radio (SDR) platforms.
Develop and test complete transmitter and receiver signal processing chains.
Implement physical-layer signal processing algorithms for wireless communication systems.
Integrate hardware and software components for experimental wireless platforms.
Conduct over-the-air experiments and evaluate system performance.
Contribute to the development of experimental testbeds supporting research on emerging 6G wireless communication technologies.
Collaborate with researchers within the NYUAD Wireless Center on wireless communications research and experimentation.
Supervision
This position is supervised by Dr. Murat Usyal

jobs.title: Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor of Interventional Radiology
jobs.institution: University of Virginia: Radiology and Medical Imaging-Diagnostic and Interventional Neuroradiology
jobs.description:
The Department of Radiology and Medical Imaging at the University of Virginia (UVA) seeks applications for a fellowship-trained board-eligible or board-certified Interventional Radiologist. The IR Division has seven state-of-the-art interventional suites, including a CT scanner on rails that moves between two of the IR suites, and 16 prep/recovery bays. The Division performs a broad range of peripheral vascular interventions including: angioplasty, thrombolysis, atherectomy, stenting, and endoleak therapies. The division also performs complex venous recanalizations, filter removal, dialysis access revision, venous access, and pulmonary embolism therapies (as part of the UVA PERT team). Hepatic interventions including TIPS, -RTO, biliary work and interventional oncologic work that spans arterial embolotherapy (TARE and TACE) and ablations. Prostatic and uterine artery embolizations and other gender-focused interventions, including focused ultrasound and pelvic venous disease therapies, are routine procedures in the division. Other non-vascular work includes urologic procedures, enteric access, biopsy and drainages, lymphatic embolizations, and osseous procedures. We perform vein ablations and sclerotherapy at a freestanding outpatient center, Division members also have opportunities to interpret peripheral CTA, MRA and duplex vascular exams. There is ongoing growth of pediatric interventions, including an expanding vascular malformation practice, driven by the ongoing expansion of the UVA Children’s Hospital.
The IR Division routinely admits its own patients, provides inpatient and outpatient consults and operates a dedicated IR clinic five days a week. Three nurse practitioners and four physician assistants are members of the IR team. The Division has 15 ACGME-accredited integrated residency positions (three per year), and three independent residency positions per year.
The IR faculty are involved with multiple industry, federally-sponsored, and individual-investigator clinical investigations. The department has robust basic/translational research infrastructure, including fluoroscopy/angiography, MRI, CT, PET, and SPECT, small and large animal vivarium and dedicated lab space with IR faculty experienced in basic science, translational research, and the application process for competitive grants.
The UVA Department of Radiology and Medical Imaging has nine divisions, ~75 full-time clinical faculty, 16 research faculty, 45 DR and IR residents and ~24 fellows/instructors working in a Level 1 Trauma Center with busy transplant and cardiovascular services and strong representation in all medical and surgical specialties. The department strives to offer faculty members a positive, supportive and genuinely non-competitive professional community with state-of-the-art facilities and technologies as well as a dedicated marketing team. Our faculty are highly productive clinically and academically as well as very well respected, dynamic, educators. Many are leaders and innovators in their fields. The Department and its faculty and staff are committed to growing the diversity of all of its team members, imbuing a culture of respect and inclusivity, and supporting efforts to improve work-life balance.
We offer a competitive salary and benefits plan, relocation assistance, productivity incentives, a professional allotment and a sign-on bonus. To learn more about joining the UVA Department of Radiology and Medical Imaging, please visit med.virginia.edu/radiology/join-us/. For more information on the benefits at UVA, visit https://hr.virginia.edu/benefits.
Charlottesville, Virginia, is consistently ranked by media outlets as one of the best places in the United States to live, work and raise a family. This vibrant and enlightened small city is nestled in the foothills of the Blue Ridge Mountains and has excellent public and private schools, diverse housing options and exceptional food, beverage, music, and art scenes. The University of Virginia is a top-5 nationally ranked public university and is renowned as one of the most beautiful college campuses in America. The Atlantic Ocean, Washington D.C. and Shenandoah National Park are each a short drive away. Charlottesville is also served by its own regional airport and Amtrak service. For more information about UVA and the Charlottesville community please see http://www.virginia.edu/life/charlottesville and https://embarkcva.com/.
The position will remain open until filled.

jobs.title: Seeking Doctoral Candidates in Archaeobotany
jobs.institution: Pompeu Fabra University: Department of Humanities
jobs.description:
The Culture, Archaeology and Socio-Ecological Dynamics research group at the Department of Humanities of Pompeu Fabra University (Barcelona, Spain) is seeking motivated candidates with a strong academic record to pursue a PhD in archaeobotany, focusing on the study of plant microremains such as phytoliths and starch from archaeological contexts.
The group offers an active and collaborative research environment, with ongoing projects in South America, South Asia, and other regions. Candidates will be supported in applying for competitive predoctoral funding opportunities at the national and international levels, depending on their profile and the calls available.
Due to the high level of competition for predoctoral funding, candidates must have a minimum combined average grade of 8.5 out of 10 across the degree(s) qualifying them for doctoral studies at Pompeu Fabra University. Admission requirements for the PhD program can be found at https://www.upf.edu/web/doctorats/historia. Candidates who obtained their degree(s) outside Spain must complete an equivalence process to convert their grades to the Spanish grading scale using the following free online service: https://universidades.sede.gob.es/pagina/index/directorio/Equivalencia_notas_medias.
Interested candidates are invited to contact marco.madella@upf.edu and javier.ruiz@upf.edu to discuss potential PhD topics, research lines, and the application process.
Please submit your expression of interest by October 30, 2026, including a cover letter (max. 1 page), a CV (max. 2 pages), and an academic transcript or summary of grades. Candidates who obtained their degree(s) outside Spain must also include a copy of the official grade equivalence.

jobs.title: Assistant/Associate Professor General Neurology (RFP 202610-2414)
jobs.institution: Yale University: Neurology
jobs.description:
Faculty in the Division of General Neurology evaluate and treat all neurological conditions. They are the major access point for care for patients with neurological conditions across the region. With the launch of the Brain Health Initiative, the Neurology department is committed to comprehensive neurologic care across the lifespan, access to groundbreaking research and the latest therapies. The division includes faculty practices as well as the Yale Neurology Resident Clinics. The Resident Clinics offer specialized care in general neurology and stroke and includes the Neurology Urgent Access Clinic (NUAC). The goal of NUAC is to allow expedited evaluation of patients seen in the emergency room as well as those referred from physicians requiring an urgent assessment. Yale Neurology has also recently developed a resident track in general neurology, focused on the comprehensive training of residents dedicated to providing the highest level of outpatient care across the spectrum of neurological disorders. The Division of General Neurology is embedded within the Neurology department with the breadth of subspecialty care. We provide a highly collaborative, supportive, and mentored environment that promotes specialists to pursue career growth within their specific area of interest. This position offers applicants an exciting opportunity for individual programmatic development and goal discovery across varied academic interests within our division and department. Rank will be based on education and experience. We anticipate faculty applicants to be dedicated to the education of the next generation of master clinicians, educators, and researchers.
It is an exciting time to join Yale Neurology with the upcoming opening of The Adams Neurosciences Center at Yale New Haven Hospital. The ANC will serve as an integrated inpatient academic hub for the diagnosis, treatment, and investigation of complex neurological and neurosurgical disorders and serve as a major access point of patients requiring continuing outpatient care.
Anchored in advanced translational research and multidisciplinary clinical expertise, the Center will provide comprehensive, evidence-based care across the full spectrum of medical and surgical therapies. Through the integration of clinical innovation, emerging technologies, and collaborative research, the Center will advance scientific discovery while delivering highly individualized treatment strategies aimed at improving patient outcomes in disorders of the brain and nervous system.

jobs.title: Levitt Leadership Institute 2027
jobs.institution: Hamilton Fellowships - Levitt Center: Hamilton Fellowships - Levitt Center
jobs.description:
The Levitt Leadership Institute (LLI) is an intensive leadership education and training program promoting transformative leadership practices and social action. Specifically, the program seeks to develop students' understandings of the relationship between mobilizing people and developing social policy. Its mission is to help students recognize, develop, and practice the kinds of leadership skills and ways of being a leader that are essential for creating personal and societal changes in the current historical moment. Applications are open to all Hamilton students regardless of concentration, career interest, or class year.
LLI runs from January 11-15 (with additional optional programming on the 16th and 17th) in person on the Hamilton College campus. This year’s participants will also have an optional opportunity to apply to participate in the College Student Activist Retreat at the Highlander Research and Education Center (www.highlandercenter.org) in New Market TN during the first few days of spring break. This retreat will bring students from Clark University, Occidental, Macalester, Pitzer colleges, and California State University Fullerton learn about each other’s campuses, share challenges and joys, and think together about how to create the changes they envision on their respective campuses.
The Levitt Leadership Institute staff includes Margo Okazawa-Rey, Heather Sullivan, and other leadership experts. Margo Okazawa-Rey is Professor Emerita, San Francisco State University, and the former Jane Watson Irwin Chair and Elihu Root Chair in Women's Studies at Hamilton College, a transnational feminist social justice activist, and a founding member of the Women for Genuine Security and the Combahee River Collective. You can learn more about Prof. Okazawa-Rey's work here. Heather Sullivan's current research is on the politics of prison reform in the Americas. She teaches courses on Latin American politics, social movements, and global prison reform at Hamilton. You can learn more about Prof. Sullivan's work here.
LLI 2027 will also benefit from a special focus on leadership for transformative justice facilitated by Professor Xhercis Mendez, CSU Fullerton.

jobs.title: Assistant Teaching Professor of Chemistry

jobs.title: Manager, Clinical Trials Start-up & Quality
jobs.institution: Sinai Health System: Lunenfeld-Tanenbaum Research Institute
jobs.description:
Reporting to the Director, Clinical Research Operations & Research Compliance, the Manager provides specialized clinical research and trials expertise within the Clinical Research Hub (CRHub). The role supports clinical trial start-up and activation, including Clinical Trials Ontario (CTO) and QuickSTART processes, coordination of institutional biosafety/IBC review requirements for clinical trials, research budget development, and clinical research quality, monitoring and audit activities.
The Manager also serves as a central point of contact for complex, multisite and industry-sponsored studies, helping research teams navigate institutional requirements and ensuring that the appropriate Research Administration units, institutional subject-matter experts and other services are engaged at the right stage of the research lifecycle. The Manager owns these files at the operational level and escalates matters requiring institutional decision, delegated approval or compliance action to the Director.
Key Responsibilities
Clinical Trial Start-up & Multisite Research
Oversee clinical trial start-up and activation, including CTO and QuickSTART processes for studies where Sinai Health participates as a site.
Review study submissions and start-up requirements for institutional impact, completeness, budget and other Sinai Health requirements, coordinating with relevant institutional units as needed.
Maintain oversight of study start-up milestones and outstanding requirements, identify barriers or delays and support their timely resolution.
Serve as a key operational contact with investigators, study teams, sponsors/CROs and external partners on clinical trial start-up.
Support implementation of streamlined, harmonized and reliance-based approaches to multisite research, including emerging TAHSN collaboration frameworks, and help integrate these approaches into Sinai Health processes.
Clinical Trial Biosafety/IBC Review
Manage the institutional biosafety/IBC review pathway for clinical trials requiring biosafety review, working in partnership with institutional biosafety subject-matter experts and other relevant partners.
Identify clinical trials requiring biosafety/IBC review and ensure that review is appropriately integrated into study start-up.
Manage submissions, communication, decisions, conditions and follow-up among investigators, study teams, IBC members and institutional partners.
Maintain complete, accurate and audit-ready IBC records and support development of clinical-trial-facing workflows, guidance and tools.
Clinical Research Budgets
Support development and review of protocol-informed budgets for clinical research studies, including complex and industry-sponsored trials.
Review protocols and schedules of assessments to identify study procedures, institutional services and associated costs, including appropriate distinction between research-specific and standard-of-care costs.
Work with Research Finance, Research Contracts, Grants Management and service departments to support accurate budgets, appropriate cost recovery and alignment between protocols, budgets and agreements.
Identify budget, resource and cost-recovery issues early and facilitate resolution with relevant stakeholders.
Complex Study Support & Research Administration Partnership
Serve as a central resource and first-line case manager for complex clinical research studies requiring coordination across multiple Research Administration and institutional units.
Review proposed studies for institutional and operational feasibility, identifying requirements, dependencies, resource implications, risks and potential barriers, and help research teams understand what is required to initiate and conduct their studies.
Coordinate cross-functional discussions and provide practical guidance to investigators and study teams on complex, multisite and regulated clinical research.
Escalate matters requiring institutional decision, delegated authority, significant risk assessment or senior resolution to the Director or appropriate institutional leader.
Identify recurring barriers, process gaps and opportunities to improve research activation and the researcher experience.
Clinical Research Quality, Monitoring and Audit
Lead day-to-day implementation of the CRHub's clinical research quality, monitoring and internal audit activities under the direction of the Director.
Conduct risk-based monitoring, quality reviews and internal audits in collaboration with the REB Office and other institutional partners as appropriate.
Support research teams in preparing for sponsor, CRO, regulatory and institutional audits and inspections.
Education and Training
Develop and deliver clinical research education and training in the Manager's areas of expertise (e.g., CTO, study budgets, GCP, monitoring and audit readiness), aligned with the CRHub education plan set by the Director, including practical materials, guidance documents, templates and tools.
Support planning and delivery of training seminars and workshops on clinical research requirements, quality, regulatory compliance and institutional processes, informed by needs identified through CTO activity, biosafety review, monitoring and audits.
CRHub Operations & Director Support
Support the Director in advancing CRHub priorities, strategic initiatives and continuous improvement, including leading assigned projects and process-improvement initiatives.
Operate the Departmental Impact Evaluation Request (DIER) process for clinical studies under the Director's leadership, coordinating review with affected departments and institutional partners.
Develop and monitor service, quality and risk metrics for the Manager's portfolio and contribute to CRHub scorecards, reporting and the clinical research risk register.
Develop substantive SOPs, workflows, guidance, templates and researcher-facing resources within the Manager's areas of responsibility, working with CRHub administrative staff to support publication and maintenance.
Support non-compliance reviews and other complex or escalated matters as assigned by the Director, including fact-finding, documentation and follow-up.
Represent the CRHub on relevant institutional and external committees and working groups, and work collaboratively with other CRHub staff and Research Administration partners to support coordinated service delivery.

jobs.title: Pediatric Nephrologist [Req#: 980455, Position#: 128834]
jobs.institution: UT Southwestern: 423015 - PD-Nephrology
jobs.description:
Position Overview
UT Southwestern Medical Center (UTSW) and Children’s Health seek a visionary pediatric nephrologist to serve as Medical Director of Kidney Transplant. The Director will lead one of the largest, most established pediatric kidney transplant programs in the country, serving a diverse population across Texas and the region.
The ideal candidate combines clinical excellence, a strong academic record, and proven leadership to advance the program’s innovation, outcomes, research, and collaboration.
The Opportunity
Working with the Solid Organ Transplant team, hospital administration, and medical leadership, the Director oversees the program’s clinical, quality, patient experience, and administrative priorities. The role centers on long-term patient outcomes, program growth, and a stronger regional and national reputation.
Key collaborators include the Kidney Transplant Surgeon, the Pediatric Nephrology Division Chief and faculty, and Solid Organ Transplant Program (SOTP) leadership and staff.
Key Responsibilities
Clinical leadership and quality
• Partner with the Surgical Program Director on clinical leadership and strategy, including review of adverse events and complications.
• Champion best practices and set quality, safety, and patient experience standards aligned with Children’s Health and UTSW goals.
• Update pre- and post-transplant guidelines to minimize rejection, infection, and comorbidities.
• Benchmark outcomes against SRTR data with the surgical, nephrology, nursing, and quality teams.
• Chair the bi-weekly Renal Transplant Selection Committee.
• Supervise advanced practice providers (APPs) in the outpatient transplant clinic.
Regulatory compliance and operations
• Ensure compliance with UNOS, CMS, other regulators, and medical staff bylaws; lead accreditation.
• Contribute to risk management, budgeting, and equipment and technology decisions.
• Use data to improve efficiency and patient satisfaction.
• Advocate for adequate staffing and psychosocial support that helps patients thrive into adulthood.
Team leadership and education
• Recruit, onboard, and mentor faculty, coordinators, nurses, and APPs, and support trainee education in the Division of Pediatric Nephrology.
• Ensure appropriate credentialing, training, and scope of practice for all transplant providers.
Strategy, research, and outreach
• Collaborate with hospital leadership and institutional partners to advance program development and patient-centered care.
• Grow referrals and shorten referral-to-listing time.
• Drive research, clinical trials, quality improvement projects, and collaborative networks such as IROC.
• Represent UTSW and Children’s Health at national and international forums.
• Serve as primary physician contact for referring partners in Texas and the surrounding region; support marketing and media efforts.

jobs.title: Assistant/Associate Professor of Infectious Disease
jobs.institution: Tufts University: Infectious Diseases and Global Health
jobs.location: Cummings School of Veterinary Medicine at Tufts University, North Grafton, MA
jobs.description:
The Department of Infectious Disease and Global Health (IDGH) at Cummings School of Veterinary Medicine at Tufts University invites applications for an Assistant or Associate Professor of Infectious Disease. IDGH has a strong and collaborative research program focused on the pathogenesis of zoonotic and vector-borne pathogens, including those affecting the gastrointestinal and respiratory systems. We seek candidates to build on core strengths in the department and the school and intersect and complement departmental themes on both infectious disease and global health using innovative and multidisciplinary approaches. These approaches include but are not limited to biochemical, microbiological, immunological, computational, and modeling to investigate molecular, cellular, epidemiological, and/or organismal topics in high-priority pathogens and/or develop better prevention and treatment.
Specifically, this position will be responsible for catalyzing new research in virology and viral disease, particularly zoonotic disease and diseases of high priority to veterinary medicine. We seek candidates with expertise in the development and use of culture-based model systems. The last several years have produced significant advances in cell and tissue culture systems, including multicellular culture, organoid systems, and higher order culture techniques. This position will leverage the current capabilities and facilities for BSL-3 containment research and emerging cell and tissue culture technologies while contributing to Tufts University’s growing strategic focus on infection and immunity.
The successful candidate will promote a team approach through their scientific research, teaching, and service as part of a strong faculty whose research interests span bacterial, viral, and parasite science and medicine in both animals and humans. Cummings School is home to a variety of strong core facilities and specialized shared resources that are available for infectious disease research. These include the New England Regional Biosafety Laboratory - a BSL-3 biocontainment research space, flow cytometry, and a recently established Comparative Pathology and Genomics Shared Resource. An active clinical hospital and diagnostic lab provide additional opportunity for material samples and project collaboration. Tufts University is home to the School of Medicine, Fletcher School of Law and Diplomacy, School of Arts and Sciences, School of Engineering, and the Freidman School of Nutrition Science and Policy. The University and Cummings School are located in proximity to a rich biomedical and infectious disease academic research and industry environment.
The successful candidate is expected to establish an extramurally funded research program centered around basic and translational science. The successful applicant should have interest in mentoring and training graduate, professional and postdoctoral students at Cummings School as an integral part of their research program. Teaching in the professional and graduate training programs of Cummings School in areas of expertise will be expected.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor (tenure-track) and Associate Professor (tenured) in Business Economics
jobs.institution: Tufts University: Economics
jobs.description: The Department of Economics invites applications to fill two full-time faculty positions starting in September 2027, one at the rank of assistant professor and another at the rank of associate professor. Applications will be considered from all candidates with applied research interests related to business economics, including but not limited to relationships among firms, labor relations and training, trade and finance, regulation and taxation of firms, innovation and entrepreneurship, and key business sectors such as health care, energy and real estate. We are especially interested in those candidates with research interests that complement the department’s existing strengths in research in applied microeconomics and applied macroeconomics and fulfill the department’s aspirations for excellence in research in the broad area of business economics, with teaching and advising concentrated in this area. Both scholars will be expected to participate actively in the new business economics minor to be offered in the department. Candidates are expected to develop an outstanding research program, to provide excellent teaching at the graduate and undergraduate levels and supervise student research.

jobs.title: Director, Kroc Institute for International Peace Studies and Associate/Full Professor
jobs.institution: University of Notre Dame: Keough School of Global Affairs
jobs.description:
The University of Notre Dame (Notre Dame) and the Keough School of Global Affairs are accepting applications for a full-time, tenured position at the associate or full professor level. The ideal candidate will be an accomplished scholar, strategic leader, and culture builder that will also serve as the next Director of the Kroc Institute for International Peace Studies. The Director will lead a globally recognized institute composed of a committed group of research scholars and practitioners in charting a compelling vision for the future. This is an important leadership role that is central to the mission of a premier global Catholic research university. The Director role offers an opportunity to make an outsized impact in realizing Kroc’s mission to study the causes of violent conflict and strategies for a just and sustainable peace.
The ideal candidate will be a distinguished scholar whose research and policy engagement focus on issues relevant to the study or implementation of peace. Candidates should have a Ph.D. and rigorous training in law, history, peace studies, political science, sociology, theology, or a related field, with a record of significant intellectual contributions and academic achievement to receive tenure at Notre Dame.
This is a full-time, tenured appointment, with administrative responsibilities and teaching duties at the undergraduate and graduate levels, ideally to begin in August 2027.
The Kroc Institute was founded in 1986 through the shared vision of long-time Notre Dame President Rev. Theodore M. Hesburgh, C.S.C., and philanthropist Joan B. Kroc. Inspired by a commitment to peace, human rights, and the reduction of conflict, the Institute has grown into one of the world’s leading centers for peace studies research, education, and practice. The Institute brings together scholars from multiple fields to address some of the world’s most pressing challenges. Research areas span peace processes, international mediation, conflict resolution, transitional justice, environmental justice, nuclear disarmament, human rights, migration, religion and peacebuilding, genocide prevention, and emerging issues such as technology and polarization. In 2014, the Institute became a founding unit of Notre Dame’s Keough School of Global Affairs.
A defining characteristic of the Kroc Institute is its commitment to bridging scholarship and practice; producing interdisciplinary research that not only advances knowledge but also informs policy and action. Faculty and programs engage directly with governments, international organizations, nongovernmental organizations, and local communities around the world. Initiatives such as the Peace Accords Matrix and the Catholic Peacebuilding Network are significant and renowned initiatives to translate scholarship into practical impact. Its academic portfolio includes programs at the undergraduate and graduate levels. Supported by a substantial endowment, and a global alumni network of more than 2,000, the Institute occupies a uniquely influential position within the field.
The Director of the Kroc Institute reports directly to the Dean of the Keough School of Global Affairs. The next Director will be charged with developing an innovative intellectual agenda; continue to integrate with the Keough School; enhance Kroc’s leadership in peace studies; and foster a collaborative and inclusive community. The Director will have an opportunity to build upon the Institute’s remarkable 40 year legacy while shaping a new future as the leading center for peace studies grounded in Notre Dame’s identity as a Catholic research institution and its enduring commitment to human dignity, justice, and the common good.

jobs.title: Assistant Athletic Director for Advancement
jobs.institution: Lafayette College: Advancement
jobs.description:
The Assistant Athletic Director for Advancement will be a key partner in the growth of Lafayette Athletics engagement, communication and fundraising at a pivotal time in the College’s history— aligning with Lafayette’s strategic plan and in support of a transformational comprehensive campaign. This position will assist the Associate Athletic Director for Advancement in setting the overall vision and strategy for annual athletic fundraising and engagement across Lafayette’s 23 varsity sports.
The Assistant Athletic Director will develop and manage a comprehensive communications and events calendar, including solicitations, newsletters, invitations, and other outreach designed to strengthen donor engagement and participation. The role will coordinate all major events for the Maroon Club and Athletics Advancement, including sport-specific golf outings, the Maroon Club Hall of Fame Dinner, other key engagement activities, and will assist with the Maroon Club Golf Outing. The Assistant AD will also partner with the Annual Giving team to coordinate Bring the Roar efforts for the Athletic Advancement department, ensuring alignment with institutional and athletics fundraising priorities.
In addition to managing events and communications, the Assistant AD will manage a portfolio of prospects capable of leadership and annual fund gifts, working to qualify, cultivate, solicit, and steward alumni, parents, and friends who can make annual and multi-year unrestricted commitments in support of Lafayette Athletics.
Serving as the advancement liaison for an assigned selection of sport programs, the Assistant AD will partner closely with coaches, athletics administration, and central advancement staff to build relationships and drive philanthropic results.
The Assistant Athletic Director is an integral member of both the College’s Advancement team and the Department of Athletics. The position reports to the Associate Athletic Director for Advancement, under the leadership of the Senior Associate Athletic Director for Advancement. The Assistant AD is accountable for spearheading initiatives focused on athletics annual fundraising, monitoring and reporting on progress toward goals, and helping to ensure the continued growth of a vibrant culture of philanthropy in support of Lafayette’s scholar-athletes and teams.
Key Responsibilities:
Fundraising and Donor Engagement:
● Manage a portfolio of prospects capable of leadership and annual gifts, focusing on qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
● Collaborate with advancement colleagues to execute annual giving strategies that enhance unrestricted support through the Maroon Club and other athletic priorities.
● Support the planning and execution of targeted campaigns, including Bring the Roar, to maximize alumni, parent, and friend participation.
● Engage directly with alumni and supporters to foster long-term relationships and encourage continued giving.
Communications and Events Management:
● Develop and manage a communications and events calendar that includes solicitations, newsletters, invitations, stewardship messages, and updates to athletics donors and volunteers.
● Plan and coordinate all major Athletic Advancement and Maroon Club events, including sport-specific golf outings, the Maroon Club Hall of Fame Dinner, and assist with the Maroon Club Golf Outing.
● Partner with Advancement Communications to ensure cohesive and compelling messaging that reinforces Lafayette Athletics’ philanthropic priorities.
Collaboration and Liaison Roles:
● Oversee strategic communications and events that enhance donor relations and recognition.
● Serve as the advancement liaison for assigned sport programs, building strong relationships with coaches and program staff to align fundraising goals with team needs.
● Work closely with Athletics leadership, Advancement colleagues, and campus partners to support donor engagement, events, and recognition.
● Provide logistical and strategic support to the Associate Athletic Director for Advancement in developing and implementing annual fundraising strategies.
Data, Reporting, and Operations:
● Track and report on donor engagement, participation, and revenue progress toward annual goals.
● Maintain accurate donor and prospect records within the Advancement database.
● Support post-event and campaign analytics to measure success and inform future strategy.

jobs.title: FA27-035: Assistant/Associate Professor or Clinical Assistant/Associate Professor
jobs.institution: Southern Illinois University Edwardsville: Department of Prosthodontics and Endodontics
jobs.description:

jobs.title: FA27-037: Post-Doctoral Fellow (2 Openings)
jobs.institution: Southern Illinois University Edwardsville: Department of Pharmaceutical Sciences
jobs.description:
Type
Full-Time (2 positions)
Category
Chemistry
Appointment Status
Postdoctoral Fellow (Non-Tenure Track)
Start date
As soon as possible
Department
Pharmaceutical Sciences, Southern Illinois University Edwardsville
Location
Edwardsville, IL., USA (St. Louis Metro Region)
Position Summary
The Department of Pharmaceutical Sciences in the School of Pharmacy, Southern Illinois University Edwardsville is recruiting 2 highly motivated postdoctoral researchers. These positions focus on designing and synthesizing small molecules to support the discovery and development of therapeutics for Alzheimer’s disease.
We seek individuals with demonstrated experience in chemical synthesis, purification, and characterization of starting materials using standard techniques (Nuclear Magnetic Resonance, high-pressure liquid chromatography, mass spectrometry, etc.). Successful applicants will use a deep understanding of synthetic organic chemistry to synthesize and purify small molecules targeted to the brain. Candidates will also design or modify laboratory procedures and protocols, develop experimental designs, optimize lead molecules based on structure-activity relationship (SAR) studies, gather and analyze data, maintain notebook, and effectively report results at weekly meetings.
Individuals will receive regular guidance to ensure progress is made toward their goals. The initial appointment for this position will be for 12 months, subject to performance reviews. Extensions will be available based on performance.
Research Environment and Facilities
The research program is supported by well-equipped medicinal chemistry, analytical, and molecular pharmacology facilities, providing the infrastructure required for small-molecule discovery, characterization, and biological evaluation.
Synthetic and medicinal chemistry: Automated flash chromatography systems, preparative HPLC, microwave synthesizer, rotary evaporators, and lyophilization.
Compound characterization and analysis: 400 MHz multi-nuclei FT-NMR, LCMS, FT-IR, UV-Vis spectroscopy, polarimetry, and gel imaging systems
Biochemical and pharmacological evaluation: Plate readers, luminometry, scintillation and gamma counting, flow cytometry, and surface plasmon resonance.
Cellular and molecular biology: Inverted fluorescence and confocal microscopy, cryostat facilities, and RT-qPCR.
